hunks.baseline: Hong Dao, the Dharma King, was sitting in the main hall, nodding off, when he suddenly opened his eyes.
hunks.sol: Hong Dao, the Dharma King, sat dozing in the main hall when his eyes suddenly opened.

hunks.baseline: The first thing he saw upon waking was the small back of someone standing motionless and gazing up at the Buddha statue.
hunks.sol: The first thing he saw upon waking was the small back of someone standing motionless, gazing up at the Buddha statue.

hunks.baseline: “About fifteen minutes ago, I suppose.”
hunks.sol: “About fifteen minutes ago.”

hunks.baseline: Jeok Cheongang answered in a gruff voice without turning around.
hunks.sol: Jeok Cheongang answered gruffly without turning around.

hunks.baseline: “What do you mean, Disciple? How many times do I have to tell you? He isn’t.”
hunks.sol: “What Disciple? How many times do I have to tell you? He isn’t.”

hunks.baseline: “Oh, so you must be proud of him.”
hunks.sol: “Oh, so you are proud of him.”

hunks.baseline: “Ahem. Of course he should be able to manage at least that much. What’s so special about the Star-Array Grand Banquet’s preliminaries?”
hunks.sol: “Ahem. Of course he should be able to manage at least that much. What’s so special about the Star-Array Grand Banquet preliminaries?”

hunks.baseline: “You never did anything like that yourself.”
hunks.sol: “You’ve never done anything like that yourself.”

hunks.baseline: “There was nothing like that in my day. Back then, even the orthodox factions fought each other, calling themselves the Southern Murim and Northern Murim.”
hunks.sol: “There was nothing like this in my day. Back then, even the orthodox factions were busy fighting among themselves, going on about the Southern Murim and Northern Murim.”

hunks.baseline: “Still, this is enough to make a ghost wail. I didn’t sense your presence at all. Have you gotten even stronger while I wasn’t looking?”
hunks.sol: “Still, this is enough to make a ghost wail. I didn’t sense your presence at all. Have you grown even stronger since I last saw you?”

hunks.baseline: “Why would ghosts be crying? Buddha would be furious. The Abbot of Shaolin is dozing in the main hall like a sick chicken.”
hunks.sol: “Why would a ghost wail? Buddha should be furious. The Abbot of Shaolin is dozing in the main hall like a sick chicken.”

hunks.baseline: Jeok Cheongang turned around and shouted.
hunks.sol: Jeok Cheongang spun around and shouted.

hunks.baseline: “Who says I’m old? You should have kept up with your martial-arts training. Look at me. Don’t I look like I can stay spry for another ten years?”
hunks.sol: “Who says I’m old? You should have kept up with your martial-arts training. Look at me. Don’t I look spry enough to last another ten years?”

hunks.baseline: Hong Dao looked Jeok Cheongang over carefully, then rolled his prayer beads between his fingers.
hunks.sol: Hong Dao studied Jeok Cheongang, then rolled his prayer beads between his fingers.

hunks.baseline: “Look at this damn bald monk!”
hunks.sol: “Listen to this damn bald monk!”

hunks.baseline: “I don’t know about ten years, but three years should be fine.”
hunks.sol: “I don’t know about ten years, but you should be fine for another three.”

hunks.baseline: “Was that the heavenly patterns or whatever telling you that?”
hunks.sol: “Was that the heavenly patterns or whatever telling you?”

hunks.baseline: “Heavenly patterns? According to what this poor monk saw long ago, you should have died years ago.”
hunks.sol: “The heavenly patterns? According to what this poor monk saw long ago, you should have died years ago.”

hunks.baseline: Jeok Cheongang’s face suddenly hardened. He had read the sincerity in Hong Dao’s expression and manner.
hunks.sol: Jeok Cheongang’s face hardened. He could tell from Hong Dao’s expression and manner that he was serious.

hunks.baseline: “The heavens are vast, yet ever-changing. Just as your star was beginning to lose its light, a Morning Star rose in the northern lands.”
hunks.sol: “The heavens are vast and ever-changing. Just as your star was beginning to lose its light, a Morning Star rose in the northern lands.”

hunks.baseline: “……Jin Taekyung. So it was that boy.”
hunks.sol: “…Jin Taekyung. So it was that boy.”

hunks.baseline: “The heavenly patterns told this poor monk that a Fire King stood in the Morning Star’s path. I’ve watched for the past year, and sure enough, it proved true. Your star was brighter than ever.”
hunks.sol: “The heavenly patterns told this poor monk that the Fire King stood in the Morning Star’s path. I have watched for the past year, and so it proved. Your star now shines brighter than ever.”

hunks.baseline: The events of the past flashed through Jeok Cheongang’s mind.
hunks.sol: Everything that had happened flashed through Jeok Cheongang’s mind.

hunks.baseline: He had grown old and suffered from infirmities of old age. He had begun searching for Jangcheon, whom he had sent away long ago, to settle his final affairs before he left this world.
hunks.sol: He had grown old and suffered from the infirmities of old age. He had begun searching for Jangcheon, whom he had sent away long ago, so he could settle his final affairs before leaving this world.

hunks.baseline: He intended to personally deal with his former Disciple, who might still be committing evil somewhere in the world, and entrust the Fire Gate Clan’s future to the Sword Saint of Huashan.
hunks.sol: He had intended to deal with his former Disciple—who might still be committing evil somewhere in the world—with his own hands, then entrust the Fire Gate Clan’s future to the Sword Saint of Huashan.

hunks.baseline: Infirmities of old age were both the curse of passing years and an illness of the heart.
hunks.sol: The infirmities of old age were both the curse of passing years and an illness of the heart.

hunks.baseline: When Jeok Cheongang was about to let go of the word *life*, a hand named Jin Taekyung reached out and caught it.
hunks.sol: Just as Jeok Cheongang was about to let go of life, a hand named Jin Taekyung reached out and caught it.

hunks.baseline: That was how Jeok Cheongang changed.
hunks.sol: And so Jeok Cheongang changed.

hunks.baseline: The more he watched that talkative, reckless boy, the more the ember lingering in a corner of his heart came back to life.
hunks.sol: The more he watched that talkative, reckless boy, the more the ember lingering in a corner of his heart flared back to life.

hunks.baseline: To do that, he had to escape the infirmities of old age that gnawed at his mind every moment.
hunks.sol: To do that, he had to free himself from the infirmities of old age that gnawed at his mind with every passing moment.

hunks.baseline: Over the past year, he had immersed himself more deeply in martial arts. He learned while teaching, and gained insight through contemplation.
hunks.sol: Over the past year, he had immersed himself even more deeply in martial arts. He learned by teaching and found enlightenment through reflection.

hunks.baseline: Jin Taekyung was not the only one who had grown in the Fire Gate Cavern. Jeok Cheongang had also taken a step forward.
hunks.sol: Jin Taekyung was not the only one who had grown in the Fire Gate Cavern. Jeok Cheongang had taken another step forward as well.

hunks.baseline: “Before long, I’ll turn those three years into ten. No, a hundred.”
hunks.sol: “I’ll turn those three years into ten soon enough. No, a hundred.”

hunks.baseline: “That’s excessive greed. How long exactly do you intend to live?”
hunks.sol: “Such greed. Just how long do you intend to live?”

hunks.baseline: “I don’t know. I’ll somehow keep dragging myself along and live.”
hunks.sol: “I don’t know. I’ll keep dragging myself along somehow.”

hunks.baseline: “Damn it. Then I’ll just have to settle for ten years. So you hang on until then, too. You still need to show that you’re going strong.”
hunks.sol: “Damn it. Then I’ll have to settle for ten years. So you hang on until then, too. You still need to show everyone you’re going strong.”

hunks.baseline: “We are already waves that have flowed past. The Spear King, who was once so robust, and the Wave King, who was more spirited than anyone, have already left this world. The others have grown old enough, too. Someone whose whereabouts are unknown may already be dead.”
hunks.sol: “We are waves that have already passed. The Spear King, once so vigorous, and the Wave King, more spirited than anyone, have already left this world. Those of us who remain have grown old enough. Some whose whereabouts are unknown may already be dead.”

hunks.baseline: Some of them had withered away with the passing years. Others had died at the hands of their enemies.
hunks.sol: Some had been worn away by time. Others had died at the hands of their enemies.

hunks.baseline: Though they were called the Ten Kings, there were only eight in reality, and they were now old enough to prepare for death.
hunks.sol: Though they were called the Ten Kings, there had actually been only eight, and now they were old enough to prepare for death.

hunks.baseline: Jeok Cheongang let out a groan and shouted.
hunks.sol: Jeok Cheongang let out a low groan, then suddenly shouted.

hunks.baseline: “Cut the defeatist talk! What is this gloomy nonsense?”
hunks.sol: “Enough of that defeatist talk! What’s with all this gloom?”

hunks.baseline: But Hong Dao opened his mouth with a peaceful expression.
hunks.sol: But Hong Dao’s expression remained serene.

hunks.baseline: “By the time he finishes his preparations in Arhat Cave and comes out, he should have grown into a suitable vessel. I’ve already chosen someone to serve as Abbot until then.”
hunks.sol: “By the time he finishes his preparations in Arhat Cave and emerges, he should have grown into a worthy vessel. I have already chosen someone to serve as Abbot until then.”

hunks.baseline: The Green Jade Buddha Staff was Shaolin’s sacred treasure, handed down for a thousand years. Hong Dao had not only entrusted such a treasure to his Disciple—he had even chosen the next Abbot.
hunks.sol: The Green Jade Buddha Staff was a sacred treasure handed down through Shaolin for a thousand years. Hong Dao had not only entrusted such a treasure to his Disciple—he had even chosen the next Abbot.

hunks.baseline: The Hong Dao before Jeok Cheongang’s eyes looked exactly like a man preparing to lay down everything and leave.
hunks.sol: To Jeok Cheongang, Hong Dao looked like a man preparing to lay everything down and leave.

hunks.baseline: “You bald monk. Are you, by any chance…”
hunks.sol: “You bald monk. Are you…?”

hunks.baseline: Jeok Cheongang let the end of his sentence trail off, but what he meant to say was easy enough to guess.
hunks.sol: He trailed off, but the rest of the question was easy enough to guess.

hunks.baseline: A faint smile appeared around Hong Dao’s lips.
hunks.sol: A faint smile touched Hong Dao’s lips.

hunks.baseline: “This poor monk intends to step down after this Star-Array Grand Banquet. If the heavens allow it, I may cling to life for another year or so. But that will be all.”
hunks.sol: “This poor monk intends to step down after this Star-Array Grand Banquet. If the heavens permit it, I may cling to life for another year or so. But no longer than that.”

hunks.baseline: “The heavenly patterns… Did they say that?”
hunks.sol: “The heavenly patterns… Is that what they told you?”

hunks.baseline: “I need to rest. Please leave me for now.”
hunks.sol: “I need to rest. Please leave for today.”

hunks.baseline: Hong Dao picked up a wooden fish and began striking it. At the clear sound echoing through the main hall, Jeok Cheongang fell silent. Only after a long while did he finally turn and leave.
hunks.sol: Hong Dao picked up his wooden fish and began striking it. The clear notes echoed through the main hall, silencing Jeok Cheongang. Only after a long while did he finally turn and leave.

hunks.baseline: Of the more than fifty thousand applicants, only 1 percent—barely five hundred people—had earned the right to advance to the main event.
hunks.sol: Of the nearly fifty thousand applicants, only one percent—a mere five hundred people—had earned the right to advance to the main event.

hunks.baseline: Of course, I was among them.
hunks.sol: Naturally, I was among them.

hunks.baseline: “What does age matter? Martial talent is what counts. Still, he’s incredible. He reached this level after becoming the Fire King’s Disciple only a year ago…”
hunks.sol: “What does age matter? Martial talent is what counts. Still, he’s incredible. He’s come this far after becoming the Fire King’s Disciple only a year ago…”

hunks.baseline: “For fuck’s sake. Is he supposed to have a Heavenly Martial Physique or something?”
hunks.sol: “For fuck’s sake. Does he have the Heavenly Martial Physique or something?”

hunks.baseline: I turned toward the voice. A man who looked to be in his early thirties flinched and quietly avoided my gaze.
hunks.sol: I turned toward the voice. A man who looked to be in his early thirties flinched, then quietly avoided my gaze.

hunks.baseline: He must have thought I was going to say something to him, but he had read me completely wrong.
hunks.sol: He must have thought I was going to confront him, but he had me completely wrong.

hunks.baseline: *The kid’s got good instincts.*
hunks.sol: *The guy’s got good instincts.*

hunks.baseline: The possibilities of the System were endless. My Muscles and Bones, which had once been so exceptional that Jeok Cheongang had called them a Heavenly Martial Physique, had developed even further during my training on Mount Jiuhua.
hunks.sol: The System’s possibilities were endless. My Muscles and Bones, which had already been so exceptional that Jeok Cheongang called them the Heavenly Martial Physique, had developed even further during my training on Mount Jiuhua.

hunks.baseline: Eventually, even Jeok Cheongang had shaken his head again and again.
hunks.sol: Eventually, even Jeok Cheongang could only shake his head.

hunks.baseline: “Monster. How much higher are you planning to climb?”
hunks.sol: “Monster. Just how much higher do you intend to climb?”

hunks.baseline: “I have to see how far I can go.”
hunks.sol: “I should at least see how far I can go.”

hunks.baseline: “If this old man had possessed even half the Muscles and Bones you have, there would have been Two Gods in the martial world by now instead of One God.”
hunks.sol: “If this old man had possessed even half your Muscles and Bones, there would be Two Gods in the martial world by now instead of One God.”

hunks.baseline: “But you don’t have them.”
hunks.sol: “But you don’t.”

hunks.baseline: “……Add another hundred geun to the iron ball.”
hunks.sol: “…Add another hundred geun to the iron ball.”

hunks.baseline: I had suffered more for acting cocky, but in the end, even those experiences had helped me tremendously.
hunks.sol: Acting cocky had only made me suffer more, but in the end, every bit of it had helped me immensely.

hunks.baseline: After all, effort—no, the System—never betrayed me.
hunks.sol: After all, hard work—no, the System—never betrayed me.

hunks.baseline: The System paid out points and EXP with perfect precision, and my basic stats were absurdly high, so any martial art I used was several times more effective.
hunks.sol: The System paid out points and EXP with perfect precision, and my basic stats were absurdly high, so every martial art I used was several times more effective.

hunks.baseline: *That was how I managed to defeat three of the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes, each said to be the best in their respective fields.*
hunks.sol: *That was how I managed to beat three of the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes, each among the best in their respective fields.*

hunks.baseline: When I asked why he was going that far, he said that as long as I was there, he couldn’t win anyway, so he wanted to go home as quickly as possible.
hunks.sol: When I asked why he would go that far, he said he couldn’t win as long as I was around, so he might as well hurry home.

hunks.baseline: I couldn’t decide whether to call him simple or smart, but he was definitely a cool guy.
hunks.sol: I couldn’t decide whether that made him simple or smart, but he was definitely a cool guy.

hunks.baseline: “Alas, the martial world’s sense of decency has fallen to the ground. How could such a frivolous and violent man gain power? Oh, heavens!”
hunks.sol: “Alas, all decency has vanished from the martial world. How could such a frivolous and violent man possess such power? Oh, heavens!”

hunks.baseline: I had been listening to their endless muttering from behind me when I spun around.
hunks.sol: After listening to them mutter endlessly behind me, I spun around.

hunks.baseline: Their muttering stopped dead at my call.
hunks.sol: Their muttering stopped dead.

hunks.baseline: A moment later, the three idiots raised their heads sharply and expressed their anger one after another, each in his own way.
hunks.sol: A moment later, the three idiots snapped their heads up and expressed their anger one after another, each in his own way.

hunks.baseline: “Alas, an idiot? How vulgar.”
hunks.sol: “Alas, idiots? How vulgar.”

hunks.baseline: The Daoist wearing spotless white robes was Baek Woo, the Kunlun Cloud Dragon. I had sent him plummeting during the third assessment after stepping on his face.
hunks.sol: The Daoist in spotless white robes was Baek Woo, the Kunlun Cloud Dragon. I had sent him plummeting during the third assessment by stepping on his face.

hunks.baseline: I learned later that he had severe cleanliness issues and spent two shichen showering as soon as the assessment ended.
hunks.sol: I later learned that he was a severe clean freak and had spent two entire shichen bathing as soon as the assessment ended.

hunks.baseline: Unlike Baek Woo, whose mere presence suggested cleanliness, this man reeked of piss and was a beggar to the bone.
hunks.sol: Unlike Baek Woo, this guy looked as though he reeked of piss. He was a beggar to the bone.

hunks.baseline: In the fourth assessment, Gung Gibang had grabbed me by the back of the neck and been rewarded with a punch to the solar plexus.
hunks.sol: During the fourth assessment, Gung Gibang had grabbed me by the back of the neck and been rewarded with a punch to the solar plexus.

hunks.baseline: “Idiot? Were you referring to this Young Master? If you could explain the intent behind those words—and if you happen to know the exact meaning of the word *idiot*—I would appreciate an explanation.”
hunks.sol: “Idiot? Was that directed at this Young Master? If you could explain what you intended by it—and, assuming you know the exact meaning of the word *idiot*, define it for me—I would appreciate it.”

hunks.baseline: The last one was Zhuge Gyun, the Divine Marvel Dragon of the Zhuge Clan.
hunks.sol: The last was Zhuge Gyun, the Divine Marvel Dragon of the Zhuge Clan.

hunks.baseline: He wore the neat clothes of a scholar and a tidy hero’s headband. Judging by his clothes alone, he looked like the most sane of the three.
hunks.sol: He wore the neat robes of a scholar and a tidy hero’s headband. Judging by his clothes alone, he looked like the sanest of the three.

hunks.baseline: That was only natural, considering he was wedged between a cleanliness-obsessed Daoist who couldn’t stand a single speck of dust on his clothes and a beggar who looked as though he would happily eat filth even if it splashed into his mouth.
hunks.sol: That was only natural when he stood between a clean-freak Daoist who couldn’t tolerate a single speck of dust on his clothes and a beggar who looked as though he would happily eat filth even if it splashed into his mouth.

hunks.baseline: But as I had guessed, he was no ordinary eccentric.
hunks.sol: But as anyone could have guessed, he was no ordinary eccentric either.

hunks.baseline: He had expressed considerable regret over losing in the mechanisms-and-formations assessment, the fifth one.
hunks.sol: He had expressed considerable displeasure over losing the fifth assessment, mechanisms and formations.

hunks.baseline: *Look at this lineup…*
hunks.sol: *Just look at this lineup…*

hunks.baseline: A group more stacked than Manchester United’s squad under Sir Alex Ferguson.
hunks.sol: A roster more stacked than Manchester United under Sir Alex Ferguson.

hunks.baseline: Standing those three side by side made my breath catch and my eyes go dark. After taking a moment to steady my breathing, I opened my mouth.
hunks.sol: Seeing the three of them lined up together made my breath catch and my vision go dark. I took a moment to compose myself before speaking.

hunks.baseline: “Everyone shut your mouths. Stop chattering and making a racket.”
hunks.sol: “Shut your mouths, all of you. Stop chattering. You’re driving me crazy.”

hunks.baseline: “Alas, did you just say ‘shut your mouths’? Fellow Daoist Jin Taekyung, how can every word you speak be so vulgar?”
hunks.sol: “Alas, did you just say ‘shut your mouths’? Fellow Daoist Jin Taekyung, how can every word out of your mouth be so vulgar?”

hunks.baseline: “A bastard who wouldn’t feel satisfied even after being rolled up in a mat, hung from a post, and beaten with a dog cudgel for forty-five days.”
hunks.sol: “You bastard who wouldn’t learn his lesson even if you were rolled up in a mat, hung up, and beaten with a dog cudgel for forty-five days.”

hunks.baseline: “‘Shut your mouths. Stop chattering…’ Those aren’t terms commonly used in our family. I was personally curious, so could you write down some of the words you use often and give me a copy?”
hunks.sol: “‘Shut your mouths. Stop chattering…’ Those are not expressions commonly used in our family. I am personally quite curious, so could you write down some of the words you often use and give me a copy?”

hunks.baseline: I wanted to beat the crap out of all three of them.
hunks.sol: God, I wanted to beat the crap out of all three of them.

hunks.baseline: Regretting that reality prevented me from doing so, I spoke to the three idiots.
hunks.sol: Lamenting the fact that reality wouldn’t allow it, I addressed the three idiots.

hunks.baseline: “You three had better consider yourselves dead if we meet in a duel.”
hunks.sol: “If I meet any of you in a duel, consider yourselves dead.”

hunks.baseline: The three idiots had just clamped their mouths shut and begun exchanging glances when it happened.
hunks.sol: The three idiots clamped their mouths shut and exchanged glances.
Then it happened.

hunks.baseline: The sound of something hard striking the floor pierced everyone’s ears.
hunks.sol: The sound of something hard striking the floor reached everyone’s ears.

hunks.baseline: An old man soon appeared on the dais. One of his legs was a wooden prosthetic.
hunks.sol: An old man soon appeared on the dais, one leg fitted with a wooden prosthetic.

hunks.baseline: “Sorry for being late. As you can see, my leg’s in this state.”
hunks.sol: “Sorry I’m late. As you can see, my leg’s in this state.”

hunks.baseline: He grinned, exposing yellow teeth, and introduced himself.
hunks.sol: He grinned, baring yellow teeth, and introduced himself.
